title: TALITHA KOUM.
paragraphs: TALITHA KOUM.
Two words.
But in Mark 5, those two words shattered a funeral.
Let that sink in.

A house full of mourners.
A father drowning in grief.
A mother watching hope slip out of her daughter’s body.

The girl was twelve years old.
Twelve years of laughter.
Twelve years of memories.
Twelve years of a father holding a tiny hand that had now gone cold.
And the verdict had already been spoken:
“Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the Teacher any further?” (Mark 5:35)
That sentence is where many stories end.

When the doctor says the disease is terminal.
When the marriage papers are signed.
When the addiction wins again.
When the prayer feels unanswered.
When the silence from heaven feels louder than your faith.
The crowd had already decided.
It was over.

But here is the tension of the Gospel story:
Jesus does not panic when people declare something dead.
Instead, He looks at Jairus — a father collapsing under grief — and says:
“Do not fear. Only believe.” (Mark 5:36)
Pause right there.
Because faith often gets tested between the promise and the miracle.

Not in the celebration.
In the delay.
While Jesus was on His way to heal Jairus’ daughter, He stopped to heal another woman who had been bleeding for twelve years.
To Jairus, every minute must have felt like torture.

Tick.
Tick.
Tick.
Time slipping away.
Hope fading.
But heaven’s delays are never heaven’s denial.
When Jesus finally arrived at the house, the funeral had already begun.

Professional mourners.
Loud wailing.
Public grief filling the room.
Jesus stepped into that atmosphere and said something that sounded almost offensive:
“The child is not dead but sleeping.” (Mark 5:39)
And the crowd laughed at Him.
They mocked Him.
Because unbelief always laughs at resurrection language.
To them, death was final.
But to Jesus?
Death was temporary.
He cleared the room.

No crowd.
No mockers.
Just the parents…
And the still body of their daughter.
Imagine that moment.
The silence.
The tension.
The grief.
Jesus walks to the bedside.
He takes the girl’s hand.

Cold fingers.
Still body.
A room holding its breath.
Then the Creator of life speaks two quiet words in Aramaic:
“Talitha koum.”
Which means,
“Little girl, I say to you, arise.” (Mark 5:41)
And suddenly…
Life interrupts death.
Her eyes open.
Her lungs breathe.
Her body moves.
The girl who was moments ago surrounded by funeral cries stands up and walks.
Mark writes something powerful:
Immediately.
Not slowly recovering.
Not symbolic life.
Real life.
Because when Jesus speaks, death does not negotiate.
It obeys.
But this miracle is more than a beautiful story.
It is a preview of the Gospel.
Because the Bible says something uncomfortable about every one of us.
Not that we were weak.
Not that we were slightly broken.
But that we were dead in our sins. (Ephesians 2:1)

Dead in pride.
Dead in lust.
Dead in rebellion.
Dead in the secret places we hide from the world.
Spiritually lifeless.
Unable to raise ourselves.
But Jesus stepped into our death room.

At the cross, He carried our sin.
He bore our judgment.
He died the death we deserved.
And three days later…
The stone moved.
The grave lost.
Death lost its authority.
Jesus rose again — proving that the One who said “Talitha koum” also has power over the grave itself.
Which means something breathtaking for you today.
What looks dead in your life is not beyond His voice.
Your faith may feel weak.
Your heart may feel numb.
Your story may look ruined.
People may have already written the obituary of your calling.
But Jesus still walks into impossible rooms.
He still touches lifeless hearts.
He still whispers resurrection over broken lives.
And when He speaks…
Life interrupts death.
Maybe today your soul feels like that silent room.
Maybe shame has been louder than hope.
Maybe sin has convinced you that your story cannot change.
But the Gospel says something radical:
Jesus did not come to improve dead people.
He came to raise them.
That means your past is not stronger than His grace.
Your sin is not stronger than His cross.
Your grave is not deeper than His resurrection power.
So hear the voice of Christ today:
“Do not fear. Only believe.”
Come to Him.
Turn from sin.
Trust in the One who conquered death.

Because the same Jesus who lifted Jairus’ daughter
is still raising the spiritually dead today.

And the most powerful miracle in the world
is still happening every time a sinner turns to Christ and lives.
TALITHA KOUM.
Life interrupts death.
And Jesus still calls the dead to rise.
Because someone in your circle may be standing in a room that feels like a funeral.
And they need to hear the voice that changes everything.
